headline: JACKDAW 🏭 GAS ⛽ FIELD 🍆 Set For APPROVAL 📜 In WEEKS ⏰
text:
UK 🇬🇧 GOVERNMENT 🏛️ is about to BUST 💥 a NUT 🥜 on that CONTROVERSIAL 😈 Jackdaw ⛽ gas field project 🏗️ east of Aberdeen 🏙️ in the North Sea 🌊 any day now according to BBC 📺 sources and industry insiders 🕵️ who say the green light 🚦 could drop mid-September 📅 right before Parliament 🏛️ breaks for party conference season 🎉!! Former Conservative 💼 government already APPROVED ✅ it back in 2022 📜 but then a Scottish 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 court 👨‍⚖️ ruling delayed everything after environmental groups 🌍 argued the consent was given without fully considering the climate impact 🔥🌡️!! Jackdaw's owner 🏢 claims it will pump out 6️⃣ percent of UK gas output at peak production 🏭 but environmentalists say when you include imports 🚢 it's only 2️⃣ percent of actual UK use 🏠!! "We got EDGED ⏳ for so long" admitted one thirsty campaigner 👀 after the Court of Session in Edinburgh 🏰 ruled last year that both Jackdaw ⛽ and Rosebank 🛢️ had been unlawfully approved because the government failed to account for the carbon from burning all that extracted fuel 🔥!!

Adura 🏢 the joint venture between energy giants Shell 🐚 and Norway's Equinor 🇳🇴 operates both fields while Aberdeen-based Ithaca 🏗️ owns 20 percent of Rosebank 🛢️ and they estimate Jackdaw could spew 35.8 million tonnes of carbon over its 11-year lifetime 📈 which equals 90 percent of Scotland's entire 2023 emissions 🌍 but they say a more likely figure is about 23.6 million tonnes or 60 percent of that same number 📉!! Environmentalists are SCREAMING 🚨 that more drilling would be unconscionable and would totally HAMMER 🔨 efforts to cut planet-warming emissions while deadly heatwaves ☀️🥵 and extreme weather 🌪️ affect billions across the globe 🌍!! They insist starting production won't protect energy security 🔒 and that transitioning sooner to greener technologies 🌿 would be way better for supporting jobs 👷‍♂️!! Industry bodies on the other hand argue that firing up these sites would deliver much-needed jobs 💼 and improve the UK's energy security as overseas conflicts ⚔️ threaten supply chains!!

Advocates told the BBC 📺 that Jackdaw's output is CRITICAL 🚨 to extending the life of other North Sea infrastructure like Shearwater 🌊 a huge offshore oil and gas production hub that processes hydrocarbons before piping them to coastal refineries and terminals 🏭!! Adura says if approval comes in September 📅 then the field could start delivering gas to UK homes 🏠 by this winter ❄️ because construction is already 99 percent complete 🛠️!! A public consultation on the future of both Jackdaw ⛽ and Rosebank 🛢️ closed back in August 📪 and now the decision rests with Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh 🧑‍⚖️ who will make separate calls on each site!! Speaking in the House of Commons 🏛️ on Thursday Energy Minister Kate White said the energy secretary would decide in due course but gave zero hints on exact timing ⏰!!

Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently dropped that there needs to be a "pragmatic approach" towards domestic oil and gas saying "We won't be able to stop using oil and gas for some time that's just a fact" and that the real question is whether we can accelerate its use so we can actually pay for the transition 💰!! Unlike North Sea oil which mostly gets exported then reimported in refined forms almost all North Sea gas stays right here in the UK for domestic use 🏠!! The UK is heavily reliant on gas imports with over 60 percent coming from Norway 🇳🇴 and the United States 🇺🇸 while wholesale natural gas prices have surged this year due to the Iran war reaching a three-year high 📈 and sparking massive energy security fears!! Gas storage levels in Europe are way lower than usual for this time of year after countries delayed stockpiling in summer hoping the conflict would end before winter and prices would drop 🧊!!

They now face the rush to buy gas now or pay potentially higher prices when winter hits ❄️ and prices are set internationally so a green light to Jackdaw won't actually lower the cost of gas for domestic consumers 🏠!! But extracting the gas domestically creates lower greenhouse gas emissions than liquefying shipping and regasifying LNG imported from other countries 🚢!! Chris O'Shea the boss of British Gas owner Centrica said any additional domestic gas supply would reduce Britain's reliance on imported fossil fuels so it's got to be good and he told the BBC's Today programme that it wouldn't lower the cost materially but basic economics would tell you that if you've got a fixed demand and you increase the supply the price should move 📉!! He also pointed to the high tax rates on North Sea profits adding that the new extraction would give the government more money to spend 💷!!

Campaigners in London urged Andy Burnham not to open the North Sea to new projects while Tessa Khan executive director of environmental group Uplift which brought the legal challenge said more North Sea drilling would not cut energy bills and would make no meaningful difference to UK energy supply!! "The science is clear that the world already has far more oil and gas than can ever be safely burned if we are to limit warming" she added and when it comes to these decisions the prime minister needs to listen to scientists warnings and think back to those families who lost their homes to this summer's wildfires the UK farmers struggling to grow our food in the drought and the lives lost in the floods in Nepal and not the self-interested demands of the oil companies 🌍!! The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero said it does not comment on speculation but a spokesman added that the North Sea remains a vital national asset and oil and gas will continue to play an important role in our energy system for decades to come alongside transitioning to clean power to protect jobs and tackle the climate crisis!! Any decision will take into account all relevant evidence including environmental assessments and public representations received during the consultation process!!
